# The subquotient generated by a weight of multiplicity one

This module sets up the two stable subspaces `X ⊇ Y` of Tits's Proposition 3.4
(Tits, *Représentations linéaires irréductibles d'un groupe réductif sur un
corps quelconque*, J. reine angew. Math. 247 (1971), §3.4, proof of
Proposition 3.4). Fix a weight `ν` of a representation `ρ` of a group `H` with a
split pinning `p`, over any field. Then:

- `X` is the smallest stable subspace containing the weight space of `ν`;
- `Y` is the largest stable subspace of `X` meeting that weight space
  trivially.

When `ν` has multiplicity one, every stable subspace between `Y` and `X` is
`Y` or `X`. So `X/Y` is the irreducible subquotient carrying the weight `ν`.
Stability is the published all-affine-tests predicate `IsStableSubspace`.

## Stable subspaces

- `LinearReductivity.coefficientMap ρ A x ℓ` is the linear map
  `v ↦ (ℓ((ρ(x) v)_i))_i` whose invariance, over all tests `A`, points `x` and
  functionals `ℓ`, is stability. `isStableSubspace_iff_stabilityMap` restates
  the definition in this form.
- `isStableSubspace_sInf` and `LinearReductivity.isStableSubspace_sSup`: arbitrary infima and
  suprema of stable subspaces are stable.
- The published `IsStableSubspace.characterProjector_mem`
  (`MatrixRepresentation/IrreducibleOrbitRealization`) says that the character
  projectors `characterProjector` preserve stable subspaces; it is used below.
- `IsStableSubspace.le_iSup_inf_characterSpace`: a stable subspace of a
  representation that is the sum of its character spaces is the sum of its
  intersections with them. Decompose a vector into character components and
  apply the projectors.

## Weight decomposition of stable subspaces

- `SplitPinning.IsStableSubspace.le_iSup_inf_weightSpace`: a stable subspace is
  the sum of its intersections with the weight spaces. It restricts to the
  split torus (published `IsStableSubspace.restrict`,
  `iSup_characterSpace_eq_top_of_isSplitTorus`).
- `SplitPinning.IsStableSubspace.le_iSup_ne`: a stable subspace meeting the `ν`
  weight space trivially lies in the sum of the other weight spaces.

## The subspaces `X` and `Y`

- `highestGenerated ρ ν` (`X`) is the infimum of the stable subspaces containing
  the `ν` weight space. `isStableSubspace_highestGenerated`,
  `weightSpace_le_highestGenerated` and `highestGenerated_le` give its universal
  property.
- `highestRadical ρ ν` (`Y`) is the supremum of the stable subspaces of `X`
  meeting the `ν` weight space trivially. `isStableSubspace_highestRadical`,
  `highestRadical_le` and `le_highestRadical` give its universal property.
- `highestRadical_inf_weightSpace`: `Y` still meets the `ν` weight space trivially.
  Each of the subspaces in the supremum lies in the sum of the other weight
  spaces, and weight spaces are independent (the published
  `iSupIndep_representationWeightSpace` of `Rational/PathFundamentalWeights`).
- `eq_highestRadical_or_eq_highestGenerated`: if the `ν` weight space has
  dimension one, every stable subspace `V` with `Y ≤ V ≤ X` equals `Y` or `X`.
  Either `V` meets the weight space trivially, and then `V ≤ Y`. Or `V`
  contains the whole one-dimensional weight space, and then `X ≤ V`.

No assumption on the field or its characteristic is made.
